name: Metric Tree Builder
summary: Builds a north-star metric tree: input metrics that drive it, each with a precise definition and owner.
description: Proposes a north-star metric for your product and breaks it down into input metrics a team can influence, with exact definitions, the direction each should move, a suggested owner and leading or lagging type. Every metric except the north star names its parent, and parents must exist in the tree, so the result is a real hierarchy you can put on a dashboard. Who it's for: product leaders, analysts and founders aligning teams on what to measure. Limitations: definitions are proposals to check against what your analytics can track; it does not set targets or pull data.
problems: We track too many metrics and none of them matter
I need a north star metric for our product
Teams don't know which numbers they can move

inputs.label: Business model
inputs.example: Per-seat SaaS subscription, monthly or annual

inputs.label: Metrics you track today
inputs.example:
MRR
Weekly active users
Trial conversion

outputs.label: Metric tree
outputs.description: North star, input metrics with definitions and parents, and gaps.

execution.system: You are a product analytics lead. A good metric tree has one north star that reflects customer value, and input metrics that teams can move within weeks. Definitions must be precise enough to implement in SQL: event, unit, time window and filters.

north_star_rationale.description: Why the north star reflects the value customers get.
north_star_rationale.title: Why this north star

id.description: "NS" for the north star; M1, M2, ... for input metrics.

parent_id.description: Id of the metric this one drives. Omit only for the north star.

steps.name: Build tree
steps.responsibility: Propose the north star and input metrics.
steps.prompt: List the north star first, with id "NS", type north_star and no parent_id. Then list 3-15 input metrics with ids M1, M2, ..., each naming its parent_id: "NS" or another input metric. Write definitions with event, unit, window and filters. Review the metrics the user tracks today, if given.

steps.name: Check tree
steps.responsibility: Every parent exists; metric names are unique.

criteria.description: Every parent named in the tree exists in the tree.
